parsed.rationale: This tracing shows sinus rhythm at about 55–60 bpm with normal PR and narrow QRS, no pathological Q waves, and no ST elevation that meets STEMI criteria in contiguous leads (only a normal small J-point rise in V2–V3), so although your patient was later found to have a STEMI, it is not visible here; if this was the first ECG, early or evolving ischemia needs serial ECGs every 15–30 minutes, posterior/right leads, and troponin.
